subject: Chemistry
title: Monosaccharide Structures: Glucose Reactions, Anomers, & Mutarotation
topics: 2.1 Chemical Reactions & Structure Elucidation of D-Glucose (HI, NH₂OH, HCN, Br₂/H₂O, Conc. HNO₃, Ac₂O)
Diagnostic Proofs: n-Hexane (Linear 6C), Gluconic Acid (Aldehyde), Saccharic Acid (C-6 1° Alcohol), Pentaacetate (5 -OH)
2.2 Cyclic Pyranose Anomers: α-D-Glucopyranose (C-1 OH below ring plane) vs β-D-Glucopyranose (C-1 OH above ring plane)
Mutarotation Mechanics: Spontaneous Optical Rotation Equilibrium at +52.7° (36.4% α, 63.6% β)
2.3 D-Fructose Fructofuranose Ring (C-2 Anomeric Carbon) & Lobry de Bruyn-Alberda van Ekenstein Enolization
quickSummary: D-Glucose reactions establish its straight 6C chain (HI), aldehyde group (Br₂/H₂O to gluconic acid), C-6 1° alcohol (HNO₃ to saccharic acid), and 5 -OH groups (pentaacetate). Glucose forms a 6-membered pyranose ring with α and β anomers differing at C-1. Mutarotation reaches an equilibrium of +52.7° (36.4% α, 63.6% β). D-Fructose reduces Tollens'/Fehling's reagents due to Lobry de Bruyn-Ekenstein enolization.
summary: Master glucose structural elucidation reactions, Haworth pyranose anomer geometries, mutarotation, and fructose enolization.

HAWORTH PYRANOSE RING STRUCTURES
                        
        CH₂OH (C-6)                                CH₂OH (C-6)
        │                                          │
        O     H                                    O     OH (C-1 β)
     ┌──┴───┐                                   ┌──┴───┐
  H  │      │ OH (C-1 α)                     H  │      │ H
  ├──┼──────┼──                                 ├──┼──────┼──
  OH │      │ H                                 OH │      │ H

   (MP = 146°C, [α]_D = +112°)                 (MP = 150°C, [α]_D = +19°)

• Mutarotation: Spontaneous change in optical rotation until equilibrium reaches +52.7° (36.4% α, 63.6% β).
• Lobry de Bruyn-Ekenstein: Alkaline enolization isomerizes D-fructose into D-glucose and D-mannose via a 1,2-enediol.
conceptBreakdown.content: Intramolecular hemiacetal formation between the C-1 aldehyde and C-5 hydroxyl produces a 6-membered pyranose ring with two anomers at C-1: α (OH down) and β (OH up). Mutarotation is the spontaneous interconversion between anomers via open chain in solution.

quickRevision: Br₂/H₂O oxidizes glucose to Gluconic acid (proves -CHO).
Conc. HNO₃ oxidizes glucose to Saccharic acid (proves C-6 1° alcohol).
Acetic anhydride yields Glucose Pentaacetate (5 -OH groups).
α-Anomer has C-1 -OH DOWN; β-Anomer has C-1 -OH UP.
Equilibrium mutarotation specific rotation is +52.7° (36.4% α, 63.6% β).
Fructose reduces Fehling's/Tollens' due to Lobry de Bruyn-Ekenstein enolization.
